newsitem.title: USA: Meridian sees Cairn deal closing in autumn.
newsitem.headline: Meridian sees Cairn deal closing in autumn.

text.p: Meridian Resource Corp Chairman Joseph Reeves said Monday he expects the company's acquisition of Cairn Energy USA Inc to close in late September or early October following shareholder votes on the deal.
Houston-based Meridian will maintain capital spending at $90-$100 million in 1998 after the merger, unchanged from the combined spending levels of the two companies in 1997, Reeves said.

Cairn will be merged into a Meridian unit in a $234 million stock swap that combines two of the fastest-growing independent oil and natural gas exploration and production companies operating in the Gulf of Mexico, Reeves said in a conference call with analysts and reporters.

"It's a natural extension for each of us to expand our exploration base and to expand our production base. This is not just a merger of producing properties in the same region. This is a merger of two philosophies of growth-minded companies," he said.

Meridian operates primarily onshore and in the transition zone of coastal Louisiana and Texas, while Cairn has offshore operations on the outer continental shelf of the Gulf of Mexico. The combined company would have proved reserves of 164 billion cubic feet equivalent at year-end 1996, generating an estimated $395 million in pre-tax cash flow, the companies said.
In the deal, each Cairn share would be exchanged for 1.08 Meridian shares in a deal that would nearly double Meridian's market capitalization, to more than $425 million.
